There are now three days left to save up to $200 on your TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 ticket before prices increase. As we continue our countdown of the five reasons why you should attend, we arrive at a key reason that brings 10,000+ founders, investors, and operators together at San Francisco’s Moscone West, October 13–15.
Don’t miss out on securing your ticket savings before they vanish on September 25 at 11:59 p.m. PT. Register to grab yours and get a second pass at 50% off.
Reason No. 3: Connections.
The right introduction can change what happens next for a company. It might lead to your next investor. A customer you’ve been trying to reach. A future hire. A technology partner. Or simply someone solving a problem close enough to yours that the conversation changes how you think about it. At TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, those people are concentrated in one place.
Turn 10,000+ attendees into the people who’ll actually push the needle
Big events create possibilities. The trick is making them useful. At Disrupt, you can schedule 1:1 meetings, powered by AI-powered matchmaking through the TechCrunch Events app, and use the dedicated Networking Lounge across all three days. Alongside that are industry meetups, roundtable sessions, and the conversations that happen when thousands of people building, funding, and scaling technology companies move through the same space. Plus, the countless impromptu meetings that happen from running into the right person, anywhere in the venue.
Register here to start making intentional connections and save up to $200 before your savings disappear on September 25 at 11:59 p.m. PT.
Go beyond the LinkedIn profile
There’s a difference between knowing who someone is and actually having a conversation with them. A 15-minute meeting can tell you more about a founder than weeks of following their company online. A conversation with an investor can help you understand what they are really looking for. Meeting another operator can surface an answer to a challenge you assumed was unique to your team.
And sometimes the useful conversation is the one you didn’t schedule. The founder sitting next to you before a session. The investor asking the question you were thinking about. The person you meet after a roundtable because you’re both trying to solve the same problem. That proximity matters.
Make three days work for you
You could spend months trying to arrange the individual conversations that become possible over three days at Disrupt. So don’t just build a session schedule. Build a networking schedule.
Identify who you want to meet using the event app. Book your 1:1s. Leave space for the unexpected. Walk the Expo Hall. Stay for the meetups. Talk to the person standing next to you, because one useful conversation can outlast the entire event.
